details:
I tried joining a random public group.

There was lots of people in the group, 40+ or so.

But I couldn't find anyone at all in the group, as if it were a ghost town, because you can only view members who are your friends.

Of course I have no friends in a random public group I joined.

This kinda just doesn't make sense for public groups at all.

----

How it should be:

As a new random join, I should be given a sort of temporary "Visitor" role, which differentiates me from any permanent Members of the group, and can be moderated thusly.

Users in the group can decide with user-specific group settings whether or not visitors of that group can find them through the group.

Visitors could have some sort of basic access to the group, whereas members get full access and see everything.

For example, maybe visitors can only see the group information, and any "group+" instances available. Whereas members can also see the gallery, all group instances, etc. What can be seen should be decided by the administrators of the group.
title: Only being able to see your friends in a group you join defeats the purpose
